name: Cheapest Deal
description: Pick the cheapest energy tariff or phone contract for a real household: monthly usage, standing charges, quarterly price-cap changes, Economy 7, prices quoted without VAT, exit fees, cashback, April price rises, half-price promos and roaming. Every option’s exact total and the winner are checked against an exact calculator.
hook: Which deal is really cheapest once every fee and price rise is counted?
author: Gauntlet Real-World Pack

cases.prompt:
I live alone in a one-bed flat with electricity only (no gas). I want the cheapest electricity deal for the next 12 months, January to December 2027.

MY USAGE (from my smart meter, kWh per month)
Month | Electricity
January 2027 (31 days) | 253
February 2027 (28 days) | 251
March 2027 (31 days) | 238
April 2027 (30 days) | 215
May 2027 (31 days) | 181
June 2027 (30 days) | 167
July 2027 (31 days) | 146
August 2027 (31 days) | 159
September 2027 (30 days) | 180
October 2027 (31 days) | 227
November 2027 (30 days) | 243
December 2027 (31 days) | 246

THE TARIFFS
A. BrightSpark Fix 12. Fixed for 12 months.
   Electricity: 25.25p/kWh, standing charge 52.54p/day
B. Volt Simple Saver. Fixed for 12 months.
   Electricity: 22.86p/kWh, standing charge 65.92p/day
C. Northern Lights Basic. Fixed for 12 months.
   Electricity: 26.20p/kWh, standing charge 40.21p/day

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: for each tariff, work out each month’s bill = kWh × unit rate + days in the month × standing charge (for Economy 7: the night share of that month’s kWh at the night rate and the rest at the day rate), add VAT at 5% where a tariff’s prices exclude it, and round each monthly bill to the nearest penny (halves round up). Then add up the months, subtract any monthly discounts and cashback that apply, and add any exit fee that applies.

Answer in this JSON format, with every option’s exact total in pounds (to the penny) and the letter of the cheapest:
```json
{"totals": {"A": 0.00, "B": 0.00, "C": 0.00}, "cheapest": "<letter>"}
```
Give exactly one answer as a single JSON block. Do not offer alternatives: a reply that contains two different answers, or an answer that says "or", is marked wrong. You may explain your working before the JSON.
cases.notes: [easy] Exact totals (monthly bills rounded to the penny, halves up): A £824.52, B £813.48, C £803.34. Cheapest: C.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: the total for each option is everything paid over the 24 months (January 2027 to the end of the contract): every monthly bill, upfront costs, the phone, roaming and extras, minus any trade-in or sale money. A price rise applies to every bill from that April onwards (they add up: the second April adds another rise on top). Everything is exact to the penny.

```json
{"totals": {"A": 0.00, "B": 0.00, "C": 0.00}, "cheapest": "<letter>"}
```
